message: Built Texel-style automated tuning pipeline: self-play data generation (7 parallel shards, 4283 positions) + coordinate-descent optimizer
Ran Texel tuning against 4283 self-play positions; overrode 2 parameters that contradicted basic chess principles (isolated-pawn bonus, zeroed king-safety penalty)
A/B tested tuned+corrected eval params: 54.2% (subprocess, 24 games) and 51.2% (in-process, 40 games) -- weakly positive, not a clear win, but never tested worse
Committed tuned eval params (677014a) -- honest framing: modest/unproven improvement, real value is the reusable tuning pipeline
Built a fast in-process arena (no subprocess spawn per game) for quicker A/B testing; validated it against itself (50.0% exactly) before trusting results from it
Analyzed all 24 Emile Andrieu (top-rated, 2608) reference games: consistently 2-5s per move even in 95-move games, never spiking -- informs next time-management refinement
Building this activity log so progress is visible without asking
Starting time-management tightening (informed by Emile Andrieu's steady 2-5s/move pattern): reducing hard-cap multiplier and max time-per-move fraction

Caught a methodology bug in my own testing: a proposed time-management tightening looked like an 86% win, but 28/30 games ended by flag -- the clock was too short to be a fair test, not a real quality signal. Re-testing at a realistic clock.
Starting full bitboard move-generation rewrite (numba-jitted) -- the highest-leverage, highest-risk remaining lever. Will be validated exhaustively against python-chess before touching real search.

Movegen rewrite: attack-detection foundation validated (384k checks, 0 mismatches). Full move generator built (all piece types, castling, en passant, promotions). Running exhaustive validation now before it goes anywhere near real search.

Implemented pin/checker fast-path (compute once per position instead of rescanning per candidate move) -- the actual optimization python-chess uses internally. Re-running full 76k-position validation before trusting it.

Wired the bitboard movegen into search. WAC tactics still 19/20 (no regression). Real A/B: 40 games vs pre-integration engine, realistic clock -- 36-0-4 (95%), zero flag/illegal terminations. Committing.

Starting the next big lever: rewriting the search's internal move representation to use raw bitboards/encoded moves instead of chess.Board push/pop and chess.Move objects at every node. Also validated that a small trained NN eval is feasible here (onnxruntime ~7.2us/call) using locally-installed Stockfish purely to label training data offline (compliant: engine never ships). Queued as a follow-up.

Rewrote the search tree to operate on raw bitboard state throughout (no chess.Board/chess.Move anywhere in negamax/quiescence) -- 1.66x avg NPS, validated via self-play (no crashes/illegal moves) and a real 40-game A/B: 24-6-10 (72.5%) vs the previous version, clean terminations. Also added aspiration windows to iterative deepening. Committing.

Tested a tightened time-management formula (informed by comparing our clock usage to Emile Andrieu's) against the current formula: 40 games, clean result, 4-4-32 (50.0%) -- a genuine tie, no measurable benefit at this test clock. Not integrating; discarding.

NN eval attempt: built and validated the full pipeline (Stockfish offline labeling, mover-relative feature encoding, training, jitted feature extractor all correct), but diagnosed a real data-scale limit -- best validation error ~515cp across three model sizes and two data compositions, nowhere near good enough. Needs orders of magnitude more labeled positions than practical this session. Not integrating; parking the code, not the repo. Redirecting to the classical eval retuning, which is converging.

Session wrap: raw-state search rewrite + aspiration windows (72.5% validated), JIT warm-up bug fix, mop-up eval fix for a real K+R-vs-K/2Q-vs-K repetition-draw bug, LMR table + futility pruning with a bare-king guard, and eval retuning on 22,905 self-play positions -- combined package validated at 63.7% and tuned params at 62.5%, both against the prior committed version. submission.zip rebuilt and smoke-tested.

Committed a bishop-colour-aware corner target for KBN vs K: the generic mop-up edge bonus was herding the king to any corner, but KBN mate only works in the bishop-colour-matching corner. Honest partial fix -- held technique together longer (44 plies vs 34) but did not fully convert; WAC held 19/20.

Committed contempt scoring: draws now score -20 for us (mover-relative), not a flat 0, after three separate real bugs this session (K+R vs K, 2Q vs K, a Lucena position) all traced back to the search settling for a repetition instead of pressing a winning position. Real 20-game A/B vs flat-zero baseline: 6-2-12 (60.0%), clean terminations.

Committed Tarrasch's rule (rook belongs behind a passed pawn), applied symmetrically to either side's rook relative to either side's passed pawn. WAC held 19/20; claimed 20-game A/B: 18-1-1 (92.5%) -- an unusually large result for a 6/16cp term, flagged for independent re-verification.

Two Claude sessions turned out to be working this repo concurrently today (cp-54, cp-e5) -- coordinated after cp-54 found an independent 40-game A/B trending the opposite direction from the committed 92.5% Tarrasch result. Also discovered the fast in-process arena and WAC suite referenced in past commit messages were never actually committed, just session scratch -- rebuilt and committed both as tools/fast_arena.py and tools/wac_test.py so future sessions stop rebuilding them from zero. Re-running the Tarrasch A/B at full sample size before trusting either result.

Fixed a real bug: 3 rated games today (rounds 69/76/80) drew by repetition from clearly winning positions (+500cp, -641cp, ~-290cp per Stockfish). Added a deterministic repetition-avoidance backstop in agent.py plus Syzygy 3-4 piece endgame tables (~4.2MB, K+R vs K / KBN vs K / 2Q vs K and more, provably perfect play) -- both verified against the exact real-game positions and via the real subprocess protocol. Also found and fixed stale platform constants (ply cap 300->600, init budget 60->90s) and discovered a Sep 11 11:00 submission deadline undocumented anywhere in the repo. Reverted a disputed eval change (Tarrasch's rule, claimed 92.5% but couldn't be reproduced independently). submission.zip rebuilt at 4.2MB, needs re-upload.

Caught and fixed a real bug in the repetition backstop from earlier today (471a3fb): _GAME_HISTORY only ever recorded positions where it's our own turn to move (per the platform contract), but the repetition check needs the position right after OUR move (opponent's turn) -- a turn-bit in the hash means these never match, so the backstop was structurally a no-op in real play. My own earlier validation was a false positive from an unrelated confound (fresh TT). Caught by a concurrent session's independent review, verified directly with instrumentation (not just re-testing), and fixed by recording both halves of the game's position history. Also likely explains why contempt alone (e73bfb9) never fully solved the original repetition bug.

Added a Polyglot opening book (codekiddy.bin, ~16MB, human-game-derived) as a blunder-avoidance safety net for the first few moves. Tested 4 real book candidates against the 47 real curated starting positions from this session's games before choosing -- codekiddy.bin covers 20/47 (42.6%), best of the four. Verified end-to-end through the real protocol. submission.zip now 20.9MB (tablebases + book + engine), still well under the 50MB cap.

Confirmed a fix for the previously-documented, unresolved Lucena position bug (flagged as open in the contempt commit) -- it's a side effect of the repetition-backstop fix, not a new dedicated feature: plain search alone still draws by repetition at ply 13 in a real test, but through the fixed agent.get_move the engine avoids that repeat, finds alternative maneuvers, and converts to checkmate by ply 59. Added tools/endgame_regression.py as a permanent automated check so this can't silently regress.

Tried adding connected-passed-pawns eval bonus -- direct-calculation verified correct (fires exactly twice per genuinely-connected pair, zero for non-connected, extreme-value check ruled out a silent no-op), but a real 40-game A/B showed 41.2% (16.5/40), a consistent negative result, not noise (clean terminations throughout: 33 checkmate, 7 threefold, zero flags/illegal). Discarded, not committed -- sound chess concept, but this specific magnitude/implementation made the engine play worse in practice.

Added knight outposts to chess_eval.py: verified directly (correct fire/no-fire on outpost/undefended/assailable cases, extreme-value scaling exact), then real 40-game A/B: 55.0% (22/40), clean terminations, consistent upward trend. WAC 37/40 unchanged, Lucena regression still passes. Committed and pushed.

Tried backward pawns eval penalty -- verified correct on both colors after tracing through 3 of my own test-construction mistakes (not code bugs, confirmed at the bitboard level), but a real 40-game A/B showed 48.8% (19.5/40), a genuine tie with no measurable benefit (high draw rate: 23 threefold repetitions of 40 games). Discarded, not committed -- matches this project's own established precedent for ties (see the earlier time-management test).

Texel tuning experiment concluded, not shipped: unregularized tuning on ~6k positions inverted several established eval terms and lost a real A/B decisively (16.2%, 6.5/40). L2 regularization toward the current params improved it to 45.0% (18/40, high draw rate) but still not a validated positive. Not chasing further given the agreed decision-point discipline -- infrastructure (tools/generate_training_data.py, tools/tune.py with L2 support) is committed and reusable for a future session with a bigger dataset, but current HEAD stays the shipped state. No eval params changed by this experiment.

Re-attempted Tarrasch's rule (rook behind passed pawn) with clean methodology, after correction from a concurrent session that the prior 16-game 31.2% rejection was already clean evidence, not contested (the memory-pressure theory explained cp-e5's own 92.5% claim, never this session's counter-evidence). Direct verification confirmed the mechanism fires correctly on both colors with exact arithmetic. But it broke the endgame_regression.py Lucena test that was passing cleanly -- the engine drew by repetition in just 8 plies instead of converting, because the new term made several rook squares along the file look similarly rewarding, diluting the search's ability to find the one precise square the bridge technique needs. A concrete regression on an already-fixed bug beats a good A/B score by definition, so discarded without even running the A/B. Endgame regression confirmed passing again after discarding.
